subproblem.title: Cone claim (10) with the corrected constant b·16ⁿ < a (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, μ a measure on ℝ^P, E ⊆ ℝ^P, Q : ℝ^P → linear subspaces, T a linear subspace and a, b, δ real numbers with a > 0 and b·16ⁿ < a. Assume ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) for all y ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ, and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ) for all x ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ, where X(x) := {z : 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x|}. Then for all x, y ∈ E with ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_T‖ < 1/16 and |y − x| < δ/2 we have |y − x| ≤ 4|p_T(y − x)|.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (E : Set (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a b δ : ℝ), 0 < a → b * 16 ^ n < a → (∀ y ∈ E, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → ENNReal.ofReal (a * ρ ^ n) ≤ μ (closedBall y ρ)) → (∀ x ∈ E, ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → ρ < δ → μ ({z | 2 * ‖(Q x).starProjection (z - x)‖ < ‖z - x‖} ∩ ball x ρ) ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (b * ρ ^ n)) → ∀ x ∈ E, ∀ y ∈ E, ‖(Q x).starProjection - T.starProjection‖ < 1 / 16 → ‖y - x‖ < δ / 2 → ‖y - x‖ ≤ 4 * ‖T.starProjection (y - x)‖

Source: parent proof, step 7 (Claim (10)); Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, chapter-03.txt lines 227–249, with the corrected constant. Dictionary: with π := T^⊥ and π_x := Q(x)^⊥ we have |p_T v| = dist(v, π), ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_T‖ = d(π_x, π) and X(x) = X_{1/2}(π_x, x) in Simon's form (2); the conclusion says that y ∉ X_{1/4}(π, x) for y ≠ x, which is (10). In the application a = (1 − ε₀)ωₙ and b = ε₀ωₙ with ε₀ = 2⁻¹16⁻ⁿ, so b·16ⁿ = ωₙ/2 < a; with Simon's printed ε₀ = 16⁻ⁿ one would get b·16ⁿ = ωₙ ≥ a and no contradiction (the documented erratum).

1. Suppose the conclusion fails: σ := |y − x| satisfies 4|p_T(y − x)| < σ. Then σ > 0, and σ < δ/2 by hypothesis.
2. B̄_{σ/8}(y) ⊆ X(x) ∩ B_{2σ}(x). Let |z − y| ≤ σ/8. Since z − x = (y − x) + (z − y) and ‖p_{Q(x)}‖ ≤ 1,
  |p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| ≤ |p_{Q(x)}(y − x)| + |z − y| ≤ |p_T(y − x)| + ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_T‖·σ + σ/8 < σ/4 + σ/16 + σ/8 = 7σ/16,
 using |p_T(y − x)| < σ/4 and ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_T‖σ < σ/16. Also |z − x| ≥ |y − x| − |z − y| ≥ 7σ/8 and |z − x| ≤ |y − x| + |z − y| ≤ 9σ/8 < 2σ. Hence 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < 7σ/8 ≤ |z − x|, i.e. z ∈ X(x), and z ∈ B_{2σ}(x).
3. Since 0 < σ/8 < δ and 0 < 2σ < δ, the hypotheses (with y and with x, both in E) and monotonicity of μ give ofReal(a(σ/8)ⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_{σ/8}(y)) ≤ μ(X(x) ∩ B_{2σ}(x)) ≤ ofReal(b(2σ)ⁿ).
4. As a(σ/8)ⁿ > 0, the inequality between the ofReal values forces a(σ/8)ⁿ ≤ b(2σ)ⁿ = b·16ⁿ·(σ/8)ⁿ; dividing by (σ/8)ⁿ > 0 gives a ≤ b·16ⁿ, contradicting b·16ⁿ < a. Hence |y − x| ≤ 4|p_T(y − x)|. ∎

Density bounds at y and x give a(σ/8)ⁿ ≤ b(2σ)ⁿ = b16ⁿ(σ/8)ⁿ, contradicting b16ⁿ < a.

subproblem.title: A set of finite H⁰-measure is countably 0-rectifiable (parent step 0, case n = 0)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and M ⊆ ℝ^P (no measurability assumed) with H⁰(M) < ∞, where H⁰ = μHE[0]. Then M is countably 0-rectifiable in the sense of SimonGMT (CountablyRectifiable 0 M): there are an H⁰-null set M₀ and Lipschitz maps F_j : ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P (j ∈ ℕ) with M ⊆ M₀ ∪ ⋃_j F_j(ℝ⁰).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)), μHE[0] M ≠ ∞ → CountablyRectifiable 0 M
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 0 (case n = 0: “H⁰ is the counting measure, so H⁰(M) < ∞ means M is finite; each point is the range of a constant (Lipschitz) map ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P”), Simon Ch. 3, proof of Theorem 1.6 (chapter-03.txt lines 145–274), where this degenerate case is implicit.

1. H⁰ is the counting measure on points. By Mathlib `MeasureTheory.Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_zero`, μHE[0] = μH[0], and by `MeasureTheory.Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_singleton`, μH[0]({x}) = 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P.
2. M is finite. Suppose M were infinite. Let r ≥ 0 be any real number and k := ⌈r⌉ ∈ ℕ. Since M is infinite it contains a finite set s with exactly k elements (Mathlib `Set.Infinite.exists_subset_card_eq`). Singletons are closed, hence Borel, so by finite additivity μH[0](s) = Σ_{x∈s} μH[0]({x}) = k (Mathlib `MeasureTheory.sum_measure_singleton`). By monotonicity μH[0](M) ≥ μH[0](s) = k ≥ r. As r ≥ 0 was arbitrary, μH[0](M) = ∞, i.e. H⁰(M) = ∞, contradicting the hypothesis H⁰(M) ≠ ∞. Hence M is finite, in particular countable.
3. Points are Lipschitz images of ℝ⁰. For x ∈ ℝ^P the constant map c_x : ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P, u ↦ x, is Lipschitz with constant 0 and has range {x}; therefore {x} is countably 0-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_range`).
4. Countable union. M = ⋃₀ {{x} : x ∈ M}. The family {{x} : x ∈ M} is the image of the countable set M, hence countable, and each member is countably 0-rectifiable by step 3. By SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_sUnion`, M is countably 0-rectifiable. ∎
proof_key_steps: μHE[0] = μH[0] and μH[0]{x} = 1.
An infinite set contains k-element subsets of measure k for every k, so H⁰(M) < ∞ forces M finite.
Each point is the range of a constant 0-Lipschitz map ℝ⁰ → ℝ^P.
A countable union of countably 0-rectifiable sets is countably 0-rectifiable.

audit.reason: The prose and type agree without assuming measurability of M. Arbitrarily large finite subsets force an infinite set to have infinite H⁰-measure; constant maps and countable union closure then prove the stated conclusion.

subproblem.title: A set on which p_T is co-Lipschitz lies in one Lipschitz image of ℝⁿ (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, Lipschitz graphs; Ch. 2, 1.2)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, T a linear subspace of ℝ^P with dim T = n, D ⊆ ℝ^P and C ∈ ℝ such that |y − x| ≤ C|p_T(y − x)| for all x, y ∈ D. Then there is a Lipschitz map F : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with D ⊆ F(ℝⁿ).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (T : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (D : Set (Euclid P)) (C : ℝ), Module.finrank ℝ T = n → (∀ x ∈ D, ∀ y ∈ D, ‖y - x‖ ≤ C * ‖T.starProjection (y - x)‖) → ∃ F : Euclid n → Euclid P, (∃ K : NNReal, LipschitzWith K F) ∧ D ⊆ range F
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 8 (“p_j is injective on D and h : p_j(D) → π_j, h(p_j x) := p_{π_j}x, is 4-Lipschitz. Extend h ... (McShane extension of each coordinate ...) ... D ⊆ F_{j,x₀}(ℝⁿ)”); Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, chapter-03.txt lines 249–262 (Ej ∩ B_{δ/4}(x₀) ⊆ Q^T(graph f) via the extension theorem 1.2 of Ch. 2). subproblem.title: Finite ε-net of n-planes in projection operator norm (Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, choice of π₁,…,π_N)
subproblem.statement: For all P, n ∈ ℕ and ε > 0 there are N ∈ ℕ and n-dimensional linear subspaces T₁,…,T_N of ℝ^P such that every n-dimensional linear subspace Q of ℝ^P satisfies ‖p_Q − p_{T_j}‖ < ε for some j, where p_V is the orthogonal projection onto V and ‖·‖ the operator norm.

Source: parent proof, step 6 (“The set of orthogonal projections of rank ℓ is compact in the space of linear maps, so there are ℓ-dimensional subspaces π₁,…,π_N such that every ℓ-dimensional π has ‖p_π − p_{π_j}‖ < 1/16 for some j”); Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, chapter-03.txt lines 220–226. We state it for the n-dimensional complements T_j = π_j^⊥: since p_{π^⊥} = I − p_π, ‖p_{π^⊥} − p_{π'^⊥}‖ = ‖p_π − p_{π'}‖ = d(π, π') in Simon's notation (3), so the two formulations are equivalent; the sibling uses ε = 1/16.

1. Let S := {p_Q : Q an n-dimensional subspace of ℝ^P} ⊆ L(ℝ^P), the finite-dimensional normed space of linear maps with the operator norm.
2. Every orthogonal projection has norm ≤ 1 (Mathlib `Submodule.starProjection_norm_le`), so S ⊆ B̄₁(0).
3. L(ℝ^P) is finite-dimensional, hence proper; so B̄₁(0) is compact, hence totally bounded, and so is its subset S.
4. By total boundedness there is a finite set t ⊆ S with S ⊆ ⋃_{L∈t} B_ε(L) (Mathlib `finite_approx_of_totallyBounded`).
5. Every L ∈ t equals p_{T_L} for some n-dimensional subspace T_L (choose one). Enumerate t as L₁,…,L_N and put T_j := T_{L_j}; each T_j is n-dimensional.
6. If Q is n-dimensional then p_Q ∈ S, so ‖p_Q − L_j‖ < ε for some j, i.e. ‖p_Q − p_{T_j}‖ < ε. (If ℝ^P has no n-dimensional subspace, S = t = ∅ and N = 0 works vacuously.) ∎
proof_key_steps: The set S of rank-n orthogonal projections lies in the closed unit ball of the finite-dimensional space L(ℝ^P).
Hence S is totally bounded: finitely many points of S are ε-dense in S.
Write those points as projections p_{T_j} with dim T_j = n.

subproblem.title: Vanishing density of M in the cone X_{1/2}(TₓM^⊥, x) at an approximate tangent point (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3), formula (6))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, M ⊆ ℝ^P with Hⁿ(M) < ∞ (Hⁿ = μHE[n]), x ∈ ℝ^P and Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P which is the approximate tangent space of M at x (SimonGMT HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q). Let X(x) := {z ∈ ℝ^P : 2|p_Q(z − x)| < |z − x|}, p_Q the orthogonal projection onto Q (this is Simon's cone X_{1/2}(Q^⊥, x) in the form (2), since dist(v, Q^⊥) = |p_Q v|). Then for every t ∈ (0, ∞] there is ρ₀ > 0 such that Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ t ρⁿ for all 0 < ρ < ρ₀.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), 0 < n → μHE[n] M ≠ ∞ → HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q → ∀ t : ℝ≥0∞, 0 < t → ∀ᶠ ρ in 𝓝[>] (0 : ℝ), μHE[n] (M ∩ ({z | 2 * ‖Q.starProjection (z - x)‖ < ‖z - x‖} ∩ ball x ρ)) ≤ t * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 2, formula (6) (“With F' := X̄ ∩ B̄₁ ... F' ∩ Q(x) = {0} and Hⁿ({0}) = 0 (n ≥ 1), so μ(X_{1/2}(π_x, x) ∩ B_ρ(x))/(ωₙρⁿ) → 0”), i.e. Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.5(3), second half (chapter-03.txt lines 96–107: “similarly by taking functions f : ℝ^{n+ℓ} → [0,1] ∈ C_c approximating the indicator function of X_{1/2}((TₓM)^⊥, 0) ∩ B₁(0)”), and formula (6) at line 184. We approximate that indicator from above by an explicit f ∈ C_c. Write X := {y : 2|p_Q y| < |y|} (open) and η_{x,r}(y) = r⁻¹(y − x).

0. If t = ∞ the claim is trivial, because ρⁿ > 0 for ρ > 0 makes the right side ∞. Assume 0 < t < ∞.
1. Smallness on the plane. dim Q = n. An orthonormal basis of Q gives a linear isometry j : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with range Q, and j(B̄_r(0)) = Q ∩ B̄_r(0). Since Hⁿ is isometry invariant and equals Lebesgue measure on ℝⁿ, Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_r(0)) = Lⁿ(B̄_r(0)) = rⁿ ωₙ for r > 0, where ωₙ = Lⁿ(B₁(0)) < ∞ (Mathlib `Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image`, `EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume`, `Measure.addHaar_closedBall`; ℝⁿ is nontrivial as n ≥ 1). As n ≥ 1, rⁿωₙ → 0 when r → 0; fix s > 0 with Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_{4s}(0)) < t.
2. Test function. Let h(y) := (3/4)|y| − |p_Q y|, φ(y) := max(0, min(1, 1 + h(y)/s)), χ(y) := max(0, min(1, 2 − |y|)) and f := φ·χ. Then f is continuous, 0 ≤ f ≤ 1, and f = 0 outside B̄₂(0); so f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).
 (a) f = 1 on X ∩ B₁(0): if 2|p_Q y| < |y| and |y| < 1 then h(y) > (3/4)|y| − |y|/2 = |y|/4 ≥ 0, so φ(y) = 1, and χ(y) = 1 because |y| ≤ 1.
 (b) On Q, f vanishes outside B̄_{4s}(0): for y ∈ Q we have p_Q y = y, so h(y) = −|y|/4 and 1 + h(y)/s = 1 − |y|/(4s) < 0 when |y| > 4s, whence φ(y) = 0.
3. The limit is small. Hⁿ⌞Q is finite on compact sets (SimonGMT `regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule`), so f is Hⁿ⌞Q-integrable and L := ∫_Q f dHⁿ ≥ 0 satisfies ofReal(L) = ∫ ofReal(f) d(Hⁿ⌞Q) ≤ ∫ 1_{B̄_{4s}(0)} d(Hⁿ⌞Q) = Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_{4s}(0)) < t by (b) and f ≤ 1; hence L < t (as real numbers, t < ∞). By the definition of approximate tangent space, I(r) := ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f dHⁿ → L as r ↓ 0, so I(r) < t for all sufficiently small r > 0.
4. Comparison for fixed r > 0. By the scaling lemma (sibling blowup_scaling), Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(M)) = r⁻ⁿHⁿ(M) < ∞, so Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M) is a finite measure, the bounded continuous compactly supported f is integrable for it, and since f ≥ 0, ofReal(I(r)) = ∫ ofReal(f) d(Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M)). By (a), 1_{X∩B₁(0)} ≤ ofReal∘f, and X ∩ B₁(0) is open, so Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(M) ∩ X ∩ B₁(0)) = (Hⁿ⌞η_{x,r}(M))(X ∩ B₁(0)) ≤ ofReal(I(r)).
5. Rescaling the set. For z ∈ ℝ^P and r > 0: η_{x,r}(z) = r⁻¹(z − x), |p_Q(η_{x,r}(z))| = r⁻¹|p_Q(z − x)| and |η_{x,r}(z)| = r⁻¹|z − x|; hence η_{x,r}(z) ∈ X ⇔ 2|p_Q(z − x)| < |z − x| ⇔ z ∈ X(x), and η_{x,r}(z) ∈ B₁(0) ⇔ |z − x| < r. Therefore η_{x,r}(M) ∩ X ∩ B₁(0) = η_{x,r}(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)), and by blowup_scaling its Hⁿ-measure equals ofReal(r⁻ⁿ) Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)).
6. Conclusion. For all sufficiently small r > 0, steps 3–5 give ofReal(r⁻ⁿ) Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ ofReal(I(r)) ≤ t. Multiplying by ofReal(rⁿ) (and ofReal(rⁿ)·ofReal(r⁻ⁿ) = 1) yields Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ t·rⁿ, which is the claim with ρ = r. ∎
proof_key_steps: Trivial for t = ∞; else choose s > 0 with Hⁿ(Q ∩ B̄_{4s}(0)) = (4s)ⁿωₙ < t (uses n ≥ 1).
Build f = φχ ∈ C_c with f = 1 on X ∩ B₁(0) and f = 0 on Q ∖ B̄_{4s}(0).
∫_Q f dHⁿ < t, so the blow-up integrals ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f are < t for small r.
Hⁿ(η_{x,r}(M) ∩ X ∩ B₁) ≤ ∫_{η_{x,r}(M)} f (finite measure by scaling, f ≥ 0).
η_{x,r}(M) ∩ X ∩ B₁ = η_{x,r}(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)); scaling gives Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_r(x)) ≤ t rⁿ.

audit.reason: The explicit cutoff dominates the cone indicator while its plane integral becomes arbitrarily small because n > 0. Finite Hⁿ(M), together with blowup_scaling, justifies integrability on each blow-up. The rescaling and t = ∞ case establish the exact type.

Simon covers the compact set E by finitely many balls B_{δ/4}(x₀); since only countable rectifiability is required we cover ℝ^P by countably many such balls with centres in a dense sequence, so E need not be compact.

1. Net of planes (step 6). By the sibling plane_net with ε := 1/16 there are n-dimensional subspaces T₁,…,T_N such that every n-dimensional Q has some j with ‖p_Q − p_{T_j}‖ < 1/16.
2. Dense centres. ℝ^P is separable; fix a sequence (u_q)_{q∈ℕ} with dense range.
3. Pieces. For j ∈ {1,…,N} and q ∈ ℕ put D_{j,q} := {x ∈ E : ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_{T_j}‖ < 1/16} ∩ B_{δ/4}(u_q).
4. Cone condition on each piece (Claim (10), step 7). Let x, y ∈ D_{j,q}. Then |y − x| ≤ |y − u_q| + |x − u_q| < δ/4 + δ/4 = δ/2, x ∈ E with ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_{T_j}‖ < 1/16 and y ∈ E. The sibling cone_claim (applied to μ, E, Q, T := T_j, a, b, δ and the two density hypotheses) gives |y − x| ≤ 4|p_{T_j}(y − x)|.
5. Lipschitz parametrization (step 8). Since dim T_j = n, the sibling lipschitz_cover (with T := T_j, D := D_{j,q}, C := 4) gives a Lipschitz F_{j,q} : ℝⁿ → ℝ^P with D_{j,q} ⊆ F_{j,q}(ℝⁿ).
6. The pieces cover E (step 9). Let x ∈ E. As dim Q(x) = n, step 1 gives j with ‖p_{Q(x)} − p_{T_j}‖ < 1/16; by density there is q with |x − u_q| < δ/4. Hence x ∈ D_{j,q}. So E ⊆ ⋃_{(j,q)} F_{j,q}(ℝⁿ), the union over the countable index set {1,…,N} × ℕ.
7. Conclusion. Each F_{j,q}(ℝⁿ) is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_range`); the family {F_{j,q}(ℝⁿ)} is countable, so its union is countably n-rectifiable (SimonGMT `countablyRectifiable_sUnion`), and so is its subset E (SimonGMT `CountablyRectifiable.mono`). ∎
proof_key_steps: Take a 1/16-net T₁,…,T_N of n-planes (plane_net) and a dense sequence (u_q).

lipschitz_cover puts each D_{j,q} into one Lipschitz image of ℝⁿ.
The countably many D_{j,q} cover E; countable unions and subsets of countably n-rectifiable sets are countably n-rectifiable.

Let a, b, ε be real numbers with ofReal(a) < ωₙ = unitBallVolume n, b > 0 and ε > 0. Then there are E ⊆ M and δ > 0 such that Hⁿ(M ∖ E) < ε, dim Q(x) = n for every x ∈ E, and for all x, y ∈ E and 0 < ρ < δ: ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ), where X(x) := {z : 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x|}.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 3–5 (Lusin, Egorov, uniform density bounds); Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6 “⇐”, chapter-03.txt lines 168–219 (choice of the closed set F in (4), the densities (5)–(6), the functions f_k, q_k and (7), Egoroff's theorem (8) and the uniform bounds (9)). The parent applies this with a = (1 − ε₀)ωₙ, b = ε₀ωₙ, ε₀ = 2⁻¹16⁻ⁿ (the corrected constant). Throughout μ := Hⁿ⌞M is a finite Borel measure on ℝ^P (Hⁿ(M) < ∞), and for every S ⊆ M we have μ(S) = Hⁿ(S ∩ M) = Hⁿ(S) (Mathlib `Measure.restrict_apply'`, M Borel).

1. A Borel set of good points. Since x ↦ p_{Q(x)} is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, there is a strongly measurable (Borel) g : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P) with g(x) = p_{Q(x)} for μ-a.e. x. Hence the set Z of points x ∈ M at which g(x) ≠ p_{Q(x)} or M has no approximate tangent space Q(x) at x is μ-null, so Hⁿ(Z) = μ(Z) = 0. Choose a Borel set N ⊇ Z with Hⁿ(N) = 0 (Mathlib `exists_measurable_superset_of_null`) and put M₁ := M ∖ N. Then M₁ is Borel, Hⁿ(M ∖ M₁) = 0, and every x ∈ M₁ satisfies g(x) = p_{Q(x)} and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q(x); in particular dim Q(x) = n.
2. Lusin: continuity of the plane field on a large closed set (the closed set F of Simon's (4)). L(ℝ^P) is a finite-dimensional normed space, hence second countable, and carries its Borel σ-algebra; g is measurable (being strongly measurable). Apply the sibling lusin (Lusin's theorem) to the measure μ, the Borel set A := M₁ (μ(M₁) < ∞), the map g : ℝ^P → L(ℝ^P) and the tolerance ofReal(ε/3) ≠ 0: there is a compact K ⊆ M₁ with μ(M₁ ∖ K) < ε/3 on which g is continuous. Put F := K; F is compact, hence closed, F ⊆ M₁ and μ(M₁ ∖ F) < ε/3. Since g(x) = p_{Q(x)} for x ∈ F ⊆ M₁, the map x ↦ p_{Q(x)} is continuous on F in the operator norm.
3. Pointwise eventual bounds ((5), (6), (7) of the source). Let x ∈ F. By the lower density lemma (sibling lower_density, applied with c := ofReal(a) < ωₙ, n ≥ 1) there is ρ₁(x) > 0 with ofReal(a)·ofReal(ρⁿ) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) for 0 < ρ < ρ₁(x). By the cone density lemma (sibling cone_density, applied with t := ofReal(b) > 0, using n ≥ 1 and Hⁿ(M) < ∞) there is ρ₂(x) > 0 with Hⁿ(M ∩ X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(b)·ofReal(ρⁿ) for 0 < ρ < ρ₂(x). Now ofReal(a)ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(aρⁿ) if a ≥ 0, while ofReal(aρⁿ) = 0 if a < 0, and ofReal(b)ofReal(ρⁿ) = ofReal(bρⁿ). Since Hⁿ(M ∩ S) = μ(S) for Borel S, we get, for 0 < ρ < min(ρ₁(x), ρ₂(x)): ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(x)) and μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ).
4. The sets of uniformity (the source's f_k, q_k). For k ∈ ℕ put δ_k := 1/(k + 1) and
  A_k := {y ∈ ℝ^P : ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)) for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)},
  C_k := {x ∈ F : μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ) for all ρ ∈ (0, δ_k)},
  G_k := A_k ∩ C_k ⊆ F.
 (i) A_k is closed. Fix ρ > 0, s ∈ [0, ∞) and let y_i → y with μ(B̄_ρ(y_i)) ≥ s for all i. If z ∉ B̄_ρ(y) then |z − y| > ρ, so |z − y_i| > ρ for all large i; thus the indicator of U := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y) is ≤ liminf_i of the indicators of U_i := ℝ^P ∖ B̄_ρ(y_i) (Borel sets), and Fatou's lemma gives μ(U) ≤ liminf_i μ(U_i) ≤ μ(ℝ^P) − s. As μ is finite, μ(B̄_ρ(y)) = μ(ℝ^P) − μ(U) ≥ s. So {y : μ(B̄_ρ(y)) ≥ s} is sequentially closed, hence closed, and A_k is an intersection of such sets.
 (ii) C_k is closed. Fix ρ > 0, s ∈ [0, ∞) and let x_i ∈ F, x_i → x, with μ(X(x_i) ∩ B_ρ(x_i)) ≤ s. Then x ∈ F because F is closed. Let z ∈ X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x). By step 2, ‖p_{Q(x_i)} − p_{Q(x)}‖ → 0, hence |p_{Q(x_i)}(z − x_i) − p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| ≤ ‖p_{Q(x_i)} − p_{Q(x)}‖|z − x_i| + |x − x_i| → 0, while |z − x_i| → |z − x|; so the strict inequalities 2|p_{Q(x)}(z − x)| < |z − x| and |z − x| < ρ persist with x_i in place of x for all large i. Thus 1_{X(x)∩B_ρ(x)} ≤ liminf_i 1_{X(x_i)∩B_ρ(x_i)} pointwise; these sets are open (as X(x_i) is the preimage of an open set under a continuous map), and Fatou's lemma (Mathlib `lintegral_liminf_le`) gives μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ liminf_i μ(X(x_i) ∩ B_ρ(x_i)) ≤ s. So {x ∈ F : μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ s} is sequentially closed, hence closed, and C_k is an intersection of such sets.
 (iii) G_k ⊆ G_{k+1}, since δ_{k+1} < δ_k makes the defining conditions weaker, and ⋃_k G_k = F: for x ∈ F choose k with δ_k ≤ min(ρ₁(x), ρ₂(x)) and use step 3.
5. Egoroff step ((8) of the source). The closed (hence Borel) sets G_k increase to F, so μ(G_k) → μ(F) (Mathlib `tendsto_measure_iUnion_atTop`) and, μ being finite and G_k ⊆ F, μ(F ∖ G_k) = μ(F) − μ(G_k) → 0. Fix k with μ(F ∖ G_k) < ε/3 and set E := G_k, δ := δ_k > 0.
6. Verification ((9) of the source). E ⊆ F ⊆ M₁ ⊆ M. Every x ∈ E lies in M₁, so dim Q(x) = n. For y ∈ E ⊆ A_k and 0 < ρ < δ: ofReal(aρⁿ) ≤ μ(B̄_ρ(y)). For x ∈ E ⊆ C_k and 0 < ρ < δ: μ(X(x) ∩ B_ρ(x)) ≤ ofReal(bρⁿ). Finally M ∖ E ⊆ (M ∖ M₁) ∪ (M₁ ∖ F) ∪ (F ∖ E), all three subsets of M, so by subadditivity Hⁿ(M ∖ E) ≤ 0 + μ(M₁ ∖ F) + μ(F ∖ E) < ε/3 + ε/3 < ε. ∎
(Remark: Simon also intersects E with a large ball to make it compact; this is not needed here because the covering step of the sibling uniform_to_rectifiable uses countably many balls.)
